$schema_note: Generation brief for Court of Beasts card art. Two layers, same model as the backdrops: YOU generate the card painting with EMPTY plaques and an EMPTY name banner; Claude Code bakes the rank numbers (and the creature name for new cards) into the plaques afterwards (scripts/bake_card_numbers.py). All coordinates are fractions of the square canvas; px values apply at the game's baked 512x512 resolution.

canvas.shape: square, 1:1 - the game renders cards square

art_direction: Dark painterly creature portrait filling the whole card interior: torch-lit, near-black ground, warm gold/amber rim light, in the style of the existing 60-card set (classic JRPG bestiary meets oil painting).
The creature is the sole subject, centered in the safe area, facing forward or three-quarter, dissolving into shadow at the edges.
Ornate thin gold double frame with corner bracket flourishes around the card edge (this one IS painted into the art, unlike the backdrops).

Four EMPTY black rank plaques and one EMPTY name banner at the exact geometry below - flat near-black (#000-#141414) fill inside a thin gold trim, NO digits, NO text; numbers and names are baked in post.
No text anywhere on the card.

frame.style: thin gold double hairline tracing the card edge, ornate corner brackets
frame.corner_brackets: reach roughly 0.12 in from each corner

rank_plaques.description: Rounded near-black boxes with a thin gold trim. Interiors must be flat and empty (< #1e luminance) so the baker's digit lands cleanly.
notes: Top and bottom plaques overlap the frame rule; left/right sit just inside it - matching the existing set.
Placement tolerance: the baker searches a +/-0.11-canvas window around each canonical center and centers the digit in the card's OWN detected plaque, so a drift of a couple percent is fine.
Keep the art around each plaque from going pitch black, or the plaque can't be isolated from it.

name_banner.description: Dark horizontal strip with thin gold rules top and bottom, left EMPTY for the baked name.
name_banner.baked_text_style: creature name in gold (#d79425) bold small caps, centered, ~0.045 canvas tall

baked_numbers.who: Claude Code (scripts/bake_card_numbers.py), not the art generator
baked_numbers.font: DejaVu Sans Bold (or equivalent heavy grotesque)
baked_numbers.layout: one value centered in each of the four plaques: top, left, right, bottom

safe_areas.creature_focus: keep the face/focal point inside x 0.22-0.78, y 0.18-0.70 so plaques and banner never cover it
safe_areas.corners: corner brackets own the corners; nothing important there

generation_prompt_template: Dark fantasy trading card art, square 1:1, painterly portrait of a {CREATURE} emerging from shadow, torch-lit with warm gold rim light on near-black ground, ornate thin gold double frame with corner bracket flourishes at the card edge, four empty rounded black plaques with thin gold trim (top-center overlapping the frame, middle-left, middle-right, bottom-center overlapping the frame), one empty dark banner strip with thin gold rules across the lower card at 77% height, plaques and banner completely blank, no text, no letters, no numbers, high detail digital painting matching a classic JRPG bestiary
reference: src/assets/cards/*.jpg are the finished look (numbers already baked); scripts/bake_card_numbers.py is the authoritative baking geometry

delivery.format: PNG or high-quality JPG, opaque, square
delivery.per_card: one image per creature; file names get slugged from the creature name (e.g. 'Ancient Dragon' -> ancient-dragon.jpg)
delivery.stats: provide top/right/bottom/left values (1-10) per creature, or let Claude Code assign them to fit the rarity tiers in src/game/cards.ts
